summary.intent: Resolve all open PR review comments on PR #416, then update project documentation (deferred items, feature matrix, README, and a new filesystem specification) on a dedicated docs branch.
summary.outcome: All 4 review threads resolved (2 code fixes, 1 not-applicable, 1 doc fix), committed and pushed. Documentation branch created with updated DEFERRED.md, FEATURES.md, README.md, and a new FILESYSTEM_SPECIFICATION.md, plus a pending todo moved to done and stale/anti-feature deferred items cleaned up.

repo: Grafana Faro is the live error tracking solution (apps/web/src/lib/faro.ts) — not Sentry, which was still listed as deferred.
Session replay is explicitly out of scope as an anti-feature for a zero-knowledge/privacy-focused product.
Phase 37 implemented Web Worker encryption but the corresponding todo in .planning/todos/pending/ was never moved to done/.
Integration tests in packages/sdk/src/__tests__/integration.test.ts require a live backend; 3 pre-existing failures there are expected in CI without a running server.

The DEFERRED.md list had drifted significantly — implemented features (error tracking, web worker encryption) and never-in-scope items (session replay, production Kubo hardening) were all still listed as deferred.
Batch upload is implemented in the JS/TS SDK but not in the Rust SDK — the feature matrix needed to reflect this gap.
E2E coverage grew: 14 web suites + 11 SDK suites + load tests (was previously noted as 11 web suites).
The filesystem spec must target the most restrictive OS (Windows) for cross-platform compatibility — case-insensitive naming is the governing constraint.

code.finding: postMessage and getWorker calls could throw, leaking pending entries — fixed with try/catch to clean up on error.
uploadFiles() doc comment overstated memory bounding guarantees — corrected to accurately describe actual behavior.

Batch reads all files to memory before the SDK call — known architectural limitation requiring SDK contract change (accept File objects or read callback instead of Uint8Array); deferred, not a bug fix for this PR.

workflow: CodeRabbit and GitHub Copilot independently flagged the same issue (lazy file reading / batch memory) — cross-referencing deferred items before responding to reviewer comments avoids duplicate work.
When replying to PR review threads via gh API, use --field (not -f) for integer parameters like in_reply_to.
Diminishing returns from automated review rounds is a real signal — after 2+ rounds of duplicate findings and doc nitpicks, merging is often the right call.

Documentation branches accumulate several categories of stale data: implemented features still listed as deferred, anti-features listed as future work, and outdated metrics (test suite counts, version numbers).

friction: DEFERRED.md had drifted badly — required a second pass after the initial update because several 'deferred' items were already implemented or explicitly out of scope.
The pending todos directory was not updated when Phase 37 shipped web worker encryption — required a manual catch and move after the fact.
File edit after reading produced reformatted table widths, requiring re-reading the file with raw line numbers before making precise edits.
Push required a retry (first push attempt failed, reason not shown in transcript).
open_items: Lazy file reading within the batch upload concurrency pool — SDK contract needs to change to accept File objects or a read callback instead of Uint8Array (tracked in DEFERRED.md, originally CodeRabbit thread 8).
Batch upload not yet implemented in the Rust SDK — noted in updated feature matrix.
Five cross-platform filesystem gaps documented in FILESYSTEM_SPECIFICATION.md that have no current resolution.
All remaining items in .planning/DEFERRED.md — observability enhancements, upload pipeline improvements, code quality, and infra hardening items from phases 28-37.
